# Tutorials — road map (TU0–TU4)

**Status: in progress. The owner's answers (2026-10-31) are in §10; TU0
records the decisions in spec §11.**

## 1. The ask

The owner (2026-10-31): docs that cover every feature with examples, where
each feature's page also records the steps that run it. When a person picks
a feature, the app walks them through it in the open project: it tells them
what to do, waits until they have done it, opens the panel the next step
needs, and points at the control. Raising a clip's volume, for example:
"select a clip" → the person selects one → the Sound tab opens at Volume →
"choose a new level" → the person drags the slider → done. The same scripts
should later drive instructional videos.

Covering every feature is a large amount of work, so this road map builds the
machinery against **five model tutorials** (§6), so the owner can try
them and change the design before it is rolled out across the guide.

## 2. What already exists to build on

- **The guide.** `docs/guide/` has 18 pages, about 6,900 lines, one per
  feature area, written from the code. What it does not have is worked
  examples or steps a machine can run. Tutorials are added to those pages;
  no second set of docs is started.
- **Every edit is a tool.** Spec §7.9's parity rule means each edit a person
  makes has an MCP tool. `AgentServer.execute(tool:argumentsJSON:)` runs one
  in process on main, through the argument gate. Show Me (§4.4) calls tools
  through that path. It changes nothing in the op layer and adds no new way
  to edit.
- **The inspector can be opened by name.** Sections have stable ids
  (`audio.volume`, `audio.fades`, …). The tab and sub-tab are reached by
  `InspectorViewController.select(_:)` and `selectClipSubTab(_:)`, the same
  paths a click on the strip takes. `select_inspector_tab`'s `section` scroll
  shows that a section can be scrolled into view without writing any
  preference.
- **The view state a step waits on is all in one place.** `ProjectDocument`
  holds `selection`, `playhead`, `inOutRange` and `selectedAction`, and posts
  `projectDocumentDidChange` after each edit.
- **The dev tools already reach the chrome.** `snapshot_ui`,
  `perform_menu_item` and `select_inspector_tab` let a proof drive and see
  the app with no person present. The tutorial dev tools (§7) follow
  their pattern.
- **Precedent for runnable docs.** `docs/graphics-api.md`'s `js` blocks are
  run by `graphic/tests/reference.rs`. Tutorials get the same kind of
  check: a step that names a tool, argument, section or menu item the app
  doesn't have fails `make test`.

## 3. Words

**Tutorial**: a feature's steps, written once in its guide page. A person
can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project or
the practice project. It is the word in the menu (Help ▸ Tutorials) and in
the code. The word goes into `CONTEXT.md` in TU0. _Avoid_: walkthrough,
wizard (which suggests the app makes the choices), lesson.

**Practice project**: a small project bundled with the app, with media made
for the tutorials, that Help ▸ Tutorials opens as an untitled copy so the
bundled one is never written (§5a).

**Step**: one numbered item in a tutorial. Its sentence is what the
person reads, both in the guide and in the app. Its machine half says what
the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done, and what Show
Me does.

## 4. The shape

### 4.1 One source: the guide page's own numbered list

A tutorial is an ordinary numbered list under a `### Tutorial:`
heading in its guide page. Each item's machine half sits in an HTML comment
at the end of the item. GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide HTML comments,
so a reader sees plain steps, and the app shows the same sentences word for
word. Because the prose and the script are the same lines, they cannot drift
apart.

```markdown
### Tutorial: change a clip's volume
<!-- tutorial {"id": "audio.volume", "needs": {"clip": {"has_sound": true}}} -->

1. Select a clip that has sound. <!-- step {"spotlight": "timeline.clips",
   "wait": {"selection": {"min": 1, "has_sound": true}},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": {"$pick": {"has_sound": true}}}}} -->
2. The Sound tab is open at **Volume**. Drag the slider, or choose a level
   from its menu. <!-- step {"reveal": {"tab": "clip", "sub_tab": "sound", "section": "audio.volume"},
   "spotlight": "section:audio.volume", "wait": {"changed": "audio.volume"},
   "show_me": {"tool": "set_audio", "args": {"clips": "$selection", "patch": {"volume": 1.5}}}} -->
3. Press Space to hear the new level. <!-- step {"spotlight": "toolbar.play",
   "wait": {"playing": true}, "optional": true} -->
```

A build step (the same kind as the one that copies `GraphicsAPI.md` into
the bundle) extracts every tutorial into one `Tutorials.json`
resource, with each step's sentence and machine half.

### 4.2 The step vocabulary

**The normative text is spec §11 TU-2** (`designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`); this
section is the first draft. TU1 added `$playhead`, `$first`, `$time`, `$track`, a list and a
menu form of Show Me, `export_started` in place of `queued`, `range`'s `changed`, and the
filter's `follows_clip` and `has_transition`.

The vocabulary is closed, so the checker can reject anything outside it.
Every key is optional except that a step has a sentence.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reveal` | Puts the chrome in the state the step needs before the sentence is shown: an inspector `tab`, `sub_tab` and `section` (scrolled into view, its collapsed state not written). |
| `spotlight` | The control the step points at: a closed list of target names (`timeline.clips`, `timeline.bar.add_text`, `toolbar.play`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `inspector.tab.clip`, `section:<id>`, `clip:$created`, `sheet.export.<control>`, …). The list is the app's own table, and the checker reads the names the build publishes. |
| `wait` | What counts as done. It is re-evaluated after each change and after any view-state change. The conditions: `selection` (`min`, `max`, `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`), `changed` (a schema path on the selected clips, compared with its value when the step began), `clips` (`added: n`), `playhead` (`inside: "$selection"`), `range` (`set: true`), `sheet` (`export` up), `queued` (an export job added), `playing`. A step with no `wait` shows Next. |
| `show_me` | The tool call that would satisfy the wait. Its arguments may use the variables below. |
| `optional` | Skip is offered, and finishing the tutorial does not require this step. |

Variables: `$selection` (the clip ids when the step began), `$created`
(the clips the previous step added), and `{"$pick": {…}}` (the first clip
in time order that matches, for a Show Me that has to choose a clip).

### 4.3 The runner and the coach panel

- **The coach panel.** A small non-activating floating panel beside the
  editor window, the same kind of panel as the recorder. It shows the title,
  "Step 2 of 3", the step's sentence and the buttons **Back**, **Show Me**,
  **Skip** (on optional steps) and **Exit**. When a wait is met, the panel
  shows a tick and moves to the next step. It never takes key focus, so
  typing into an inspector field still goes to the field.
- **The spotlight.** A borderless, click-through child window over the
  editor. It draws a ring around the target's rectangle and follows it when
  the layout moves. Because it is a window, it sits above the Metal and
  `AVPlayerLayer` layers.
- **Needs.** Before step 1, the tutorial's `needs` are checked against the
  open project. When they are not met, the panel says what is missing and
  how to get it, and offers the practice project (§5a), for example "This
  tutorial needs a clip with sound. Open the practice project, or open a
  movie of your own (File ▸ Open…)". It does not start until they are met.
- **Where to start one.** **Help ▸ Tutorials ▸** has one submenu per guide
  page, filled from `Tutorials.json`. A "Try it in Frame Job" link from
  the online guide (`framejob://tutorial/<id>`) shares #385's URL scheme
  and comes after TU4.

### 4.4 Show Me

Show Me's tool form (and each tool entry of a list) runs through
`AgentServer.execute`, the path the Assistant's calls take; its menu form
performs the built menu bar's own item, the path a click takes, with no dev
tool (spec §11 TU-3). Each Show Me edit is an ordinary undo step, and
exiting a tutorial undoes nothing. Show Me does three jobs:

- it helps a person who is stuck;
- it lets a proof run every tutorial to the end with no person present;
- it is what auto-play will use for the videos (§8).

## 5. What stays out of the model phase

- Rolling tutorials out to every guide page, and the worked examples each
  page still lacks (after TU4, one batch per page).
- Auto-play and video capture (§8).
- The `framejob://` link (#385).

## 5a. The practice project (owner, 2026-10-31: build it now)

A small project bundled with the app, made so that every model tutorial's
`needs` are met in it, and kept so as the set grows.

- **What it holds:** at least two clips with sound that meet on one track
  (Split, Volume, Cross-dissolve), room above them for a title (Add a title),
  and enough length to set an in/out range and export it (Export a range).
- **Its media is made, not found:** generated by a script checked in beside
  it, so it carries no third-party footage or music and its provenance is
  written down (a `PROVENANCE.md`, as `app/Resources/Models/` has). A few
  megabytes at most; the product still has no ffmpeg dependency.
- **It is never written:** Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project opens it
  as an untitled copy (its media copied or referenced read-only, so a save
  asks where), and a tutorial whose `needs` are unmet offers the same.
- **It is what the proof runs on** (§7) and what the videos will film (§8).

## 6. The model set

Five tutorials, chosen so that between them they use every step shape the
design has. If these five work, the remaining tutorials need content
only, not new machinery.

| # | Tutorial (guide page) | Steps | What it tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Change a clip's volume** (`audio.md`) | select a clip with sound → Sound ▸ Volume opens → change the level → play | the owner's example: a selection wait, a sub-tab and section reveal, a value-changed wait |
| 2 | **Split a clip** (`editing.md`) | select a clip → move the playhead into it → Clip ▸ Split (⌘T) | a playhead wait (the person scrubs), a menu or key action, a count wait, `$created` |
| 3 | **Add a title** (`canvas-and-layers.md`) | press T or the bar's Add Text → type the words in Text ▸ Content → drag it on the canvas | a bar-button spotlight, a new clip the next step follows, text entry while the panel is up, a canvas gesture (`changed: video.position`) |
| 4 | **Cross-dissolve two clips** (`motion-and-transitions.md`) | select the later of two clips that meet → Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve → set its length in the Transition section | `needs` that the project may not meet, a submenu item, a section that only exists once the edit has applied |
| 5 | **Export a range** (`export.md`) | set In and Out (I, O) → File ▸ Export… → pick a format in the sheet → Export | view-state waits (`range`), a sheet and spotlights inside it (the export sheet has no accessibility ids today), an outcome that is not an edit (`queued`) |

The owner kept these five (2026-10-31).

## 7. Verification

- **`make test`, no app:** `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` reads every
  guide page. It checks the following and fails on anything unknown, naming
  the page and step:
  - each tutorial's JSON against §4.2's vocabulary;
  - each `show_me` tool name and argument key against the build's catalog
    snapshot;
  - each `section:` id and target name against the names the app publishes;
  - each menu path a sentence names against
    `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`;
  - each `changed` path against the schema.
- **Over MCP:** dev tools `tutorial_start {id}`, `tutorial_state`,
  `tutorial_step {action: show_me|next|back|skip}` and
  `tutorial_exit`, compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`.

  - **as a person:** it meets each wait with the ordinary tools

    the project back with `get_project`;
  - **with `needs` unmet:** on an empty project it reads the panel's
    sentence and its offer of the practice project.

  Both the person and Show Me runs start from the practice project.
- **Seeing it:** `snapshot_ui` learns the coach panel as a window kind; a
  capture of the editor with the spotlight up, in both looks.
- **`docs/manual-checks.md` rows:**
  - the ring sits on the right control and follows a window resize and an
    inspector scroll;
  - the panel never takes typing from a field;
  - a person completes each of the five by hand.

## 8. Videos (after TU4, recorded here so the format allows for them)

Every step that has a `show_me` can run unattended. Auto-play performs the
step, holds for a reading time based on the sentence's length, and moves on,
with the coach panel serving as the caption. The recorder (with Include

   267	    a second use of an id included."""
   268	    folder = Path(folder)
   269	    problems: list[Problem] = []
   270	    pages, seen = [], {}
   271	    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
   272	        page, found = parse_page(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

   291	def main(argv=None) -> int:
   292	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
   293	    parser.add_argument("--guide", required=True, type=Path)
   294	    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
   295	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   296	    if not args.guide.is_dir():
   297	        print(f"tutorial_extract: {args.guide} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
   298	        return 1
   299	    document, problems = parse_guide(args.guide)
   300	    if problems:

1	// Tutorials TU1 — the app's facts `tutorial_check.py` checks the guide's
     2	// tutorials against (spec §11 TU-2): the prepared catalog, the dev tools'
     3	// names, the spotlight target table, the built menu bar and a fixture
     4	// project's clips as the core writes them.
     5	//
     6	// Compiled AS `main.swift` over every file in `app/Sources` but the app's own
     7	// `main.swift`, with `-D FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, through `swift_build.py`'s
     8	// `build()` by `tutorial_check.py`.
     9	//
    10	//   tutorial_probe <work-dir>
    11	//
    12	// Prints exactly one stdout line:
    13	//   ANSWER {"tools": {name: {"properties": {…}}}, "dev_tools": [sorted],
    14	//           "targets": TutorialTargets.manifest(),
    15	//           "menu": [{"path": [titles], "selector": str|null, "submenu": bool}],
    16	//           "clips": [the fixture's clips, as the core writes them]}
    17	//   or ANSWER {"error": "…"} when a fact could not be read.
    18	//
    19	// Nothing binds the agent socket, opens a window or reads media: the fixture's
    20	// media clip is a stand-in `add_media` descriptor with no file behind it.
    21	import AppKit
    22	
    23	final class ProbeDocumentController: NSDocumentController {
    24	    override var defaultType: String? { ProjectDocument.projectTypeIdentifier }
    25	}
    26	_ = ProbeDocumentController()
    27	
    28	let app = NSApplication.shared
    29	app.setActivationPolicy(.prohibited)
    30	let delegate = AppDelegate()
    31	delegate.applicationWillFinishLaunching(
    32	    Notification(name: NSApplication.willFinishLaunchingNotification, object: app))
    33	AgentLane.prepareAtLaunch()
    34	
    35	func answer(_ body: [String: Any]) -> Never {
    36	    let data = (try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: body, options: [.sortedKeys]))
    37	        ?? Data("{\"error\":\"the answer did not encode\"}".utf8)

### 1 — nit

- **What:** When the tutorial comment is refused (text after `-->`, bad JSON, no string id, unknown key), `_tutorial` returns before claiming the list, so every following `<!-- step` line also gets "a tutorial or step comment outside a tutorial's heading line or list". One error shows up as N+1 problems, and the extra ones point the wrong way.
- **Fix:** On those early returns, still claim the item lines (for example, run `_items` from the next ordered list and add its range to `claimed`). Or skip the "outside" scan for lines under a heading that was already refused.

- **Fix:** Keep the tutorial comment's line number on each parsed tutorial (an internal field that is not written to the output) and report the duplicate there.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorials TU1b — make the bundled practice project (spec §11 TU-7).

    python3 tools/practice/make_practice.py

Builds the generator — `practice_generator.swift` as `build/practice/main.swift`
beside `practice_media.swift`, over `app/Sources` (the core's own ops and
`MediaImporter.probeBlocking`), through `tools/proof/swift_build.py`'s
`build()` — runs it into `build/practice/out/`, replaces
`app/Resources/Practice/Practice Project.framejob` with what it wrote, and
writes `app/Resources/Practice/SHA256SUMS`: `<sha256>  <path relative to
app/Resources/Practice>` for every file of the package, sorted. Prints each
file's size; exits 1 on any failure, the package over `SIZE_CAP` included.

The sums helpers (`package_files`, `sums_text`, `sums_problems`) are what
`tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` imports to hold the package to its digests in
`make test`; they are stdlib only, and `swift_build` is imported inside
`main` alone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
PRACTICE = ROOT / "app" / "Resources" / "Practice"
FONTS = ROOT / "app" / "Resources" / "Fonts"
WORK = ROOT / "build" / "practice"
PACKAGE_NAME = "Practice Project.framejob"
SUMS = "SHA256SUMS"
SIZE_CAP = 4_000_000  # bytes, the whole package
WALL_BUILD, WALL_RUN = 900, 300


def package_files(folder: Path) -> list:
    """Every file under `folder/PACKAGE_NAME`, no dot-files, sorted."""
    package = Path(folder) / PACKAGE_NAME
    if not package.is_dir():
        return []
    return sorted(path for path in package.rglob("*")
                  if path.is_file()
                  and not any(part.startswith(".") for part in path.relative_to(package).parts))


def _sha(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        for block in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def _relative(folder: Path, path: Path) -> str:
    return path.relative_to(Path(folder)).as_posix()


def sums_text(folder: Path) -> str:
    """The SHA256SUMS text for `folder`."""
    return "".join(f"{_sha(path)}  {_relative(folder, path)}\n" for path in package_files(folder))


def sums_problems(folder: Path) -> list:
    """SHA256SUMS absent; each file missing, extra or differing, named; the
    package's total over SIZE_CAP."""
    folder = Path(folder)
    sums = folder / SUMS
    if not sums.is_file():
        return [f"{sums} is absent"]
    recorded = {}
    for number, row in enumerate(sums.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        digest, separator, name = row.partition("  ")
        if not separator or not name:
            return [f"{SUMS} line {number} is not `<sha256>  <path>`"]
        recorded[name] = digest
    present = {_relative(folder, path): path for path in package_files(folder)}
    out = [f"{name} is in {SUMS} but not in the package" for name in sorted(set(recorded)
                                                                           - set(present))]
    out += [f"{name} is in the package but not in {SUMS}" for name in sorted(set(present)
                                                                           - set(recorded))]
    out += [f"{name} differs from its {SUMS} digest" for name in sorted(set(recorded)
                                                                       & set(present))
            if _sha(present[name]) != recorded[name]]
    total = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in present.values())
    if total > SIZE_CAP:
        out.append(f"the package is {total} bytes, over the {SIZE_CAP}-byte cap")
    return out


def main(argv=None) -> int:

1	import AppKit
     2	
     3	/// Every save of the package announced to the cache ledger, so no marker,
     4	/// waveform or voice file lands between the save's listing and its swap
     5	/// (`MediaImporter.CacheLedger`, `MediaCacheLedger.swift`).
     6	///
     7	/// This one override is enough: ⌘S, Save As, autosave and `save_project`
     8	/// all funnel through `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)`, and NSDocument
     9	/// lists the package for its lazy `cache/` wrapper and swaps the new package
    10	/// in before that completion runs. `saveBegan` waits for a publication
    11	/// already being written; `saveEnded` runs before the caller's handler.
    12	extension ProjectDocument {
    13	    override func save(
    14	        to url: URL, ofType typeName: String, for saveOperation: NSDocument.SaveOperationType,
    15	        completionHandler: @escaping ((any Error)?) -> Void
    16	    ) {
    17	        guard let directory = intendedCacheDirectory else {
    18	            super.save(to: url, ofType: typeName, for: saveOperation,
    19	                       completionHandler: completionHandler)
    20	            return
    21	        }
    22	        let save = MediaImporter.CacheLedger.shared.saveBegan(cacheDir: directory)
    23	        super.save(to: url, ofType: typeName, for: saveOperation) { error in
    24	            MediaImporter.CacheLedger.shared.saveEnded(cacheDir: directory, save: save)
    25	            completionHandler(error)
    26	        }
    27	    }
    28	}

1	import AppKit
     2	
     3	/// The app's document controller: it knows which paths AppKit's own open is
     4	/// reading (spec §11 #234).
     5	///
     6	/// **Why it exists.** A document added for a URL while AppKit is still
     7	/// reading that URL is not seen when the read ends, and AppKit adds a second
     8	/// document at the path. An agent's `open_project` reads on the lane's
     9	/// thread and adds its document itself (spec §11 #231), so without this it
    10	/// could add one while a person's File ▸ Open, Finder double-click, Recent
    11	/// row or drop of the same file was still reading, or a person's open could
    12	/// begin and end inside the agent's own read. `AgentServer.openProject` asks
    13	/// `isOpening` in each of its two main-thread steps and waits for the
    14	/// person's open; `refuseHeldPath` refuses a write to a path being opened.
    15	///
    16	/// **What is counted.** The two public asynchronous opens, which every door
    17	/// AppKit has reaches (spec §11 #234 lists them): one is added to the
    18	/// path's count on the main thread before `super`, and taken off in the
    19	/// completion handler, which AppKit calls on main after it has added the
    20	/// document, before the caller's handler runs. A reopen with no URL (an
    21	/// untitled document restored) holds no path and is not counted.
    22	///
    23	/// **A `.fjgraphic` is not a project** (spec §11 G-47 (a)): an open of one —
    24	/// a Finder double-click, Open With, a Dock drop, a browser's download — is
    25	/// handed to `GraphicImportSheetController.open(packageAt:)` and answers no
    26	/// document and no error; it is not counted. `whenSettled` is that door's
    27	/// wait for launch and restoration (G-47 (b)): no open or reopen in flight,
    28	/// an untitled project's reopen included.
    29	///
    30	/// `main.swift` makes the one instance before anything else can make an
    31	/// `NSDocumentController`: the first one instantiated is `.shared`. No other
    32	/// product file instantiates it. A proof probe compiles every source but
    33	/// `main.swift` and installs a controller of its own first, and there
    34	/// `isOpening` answers false.
    35	class ProjectDocumentController: NSDocumentController {
    36	
    37	    /// Opens in flight, by `AgentServer.canonical` path. Main only.
    38	    private var opening: [String: Int] = [:]
    39	    /// Reopens of an untitled project in flight, and what waits for none of either. Main only.
    40	    private var untitledReopens = 0
    41	    private var settledWaiters: [() -> Void] = []
    42	
    43	    override init() {
    44	        super.init()
    45	    }
    46	
    47	    @available(*, unavailable)
    48	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    49	        fatalError("ProjectDocumentController does not support NSCoder")
    50	    }
    51	
    52	    // MARK: - Launch
    53	
    54	    /// Makes the app's controller. Called once, from `main.swift`, before
    55	    /// `NSApplicationMain`.
    56	    static func install() {
    57	        let controller = ProjectDocumentController()
    58	        if NSDocumentController.shared !== controller {
    59	            NSLog("Frame Job: %@", "a document controller existed before ProjectDocumentController "
    60	                + "was installed, so an open in flight is not counted (spec §11 #234)")
    61	        }
    62	    }
    63	
    64	    /// The startup complaint when the shared controller is not this class
    65	    /// (the `Frame Job: ` prefix every MCP proof requires absent).
    66	    static func complainUnlessShared() {
    67	        guard !(NSDocumentController.shared is ProjectDocumentController) else { return }
    68	        NSLog("Frame Job: %@", "the shared document controller is not ProjectDocumentController, "
    69	            + "so open_project cannot see a window's open in flight (spec §11 #234)")
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    // MARK: - What is being opened
    73	
    74	    /// Whether AppKit's own open of `url` is in flight. Main only. False
    75	    /// when the shared controller is not this class.
    76	    static func isOpening(_ url: URL) -> Bool {
    77	        guard let controller = NSDocumentController.shared as? ProjectDocumentController
    78	        else { return false }
    79	        return controller.opens(of: url) > 0
    80	    }
    81	
    82	    /// How many of AppKit's opens of `url` are in flight. Main only.
    83	    func opens(of url: URL) -> Int {
    84	        opening[AgentServer.canonical(url.path)] ?? 0
    85	    }
    86	
    87	    private func began(_ url: URL) -> String {
    88	        let key = AgentServer.canonical(url.path)
    89	        opening[key, default: 0] += 1
    90	        return key
    91	    }
    92	
    93	    private func ended(_ key: String) {
    94	        let left = (opening[key] ?? 1) - 1
    95	        opening[key] = left > 0 ? left : nil
    96	        fireIfSettled()
    97	    }
    98	
    99	    // MARK: - Settled
   100	
   101	    /// Runs `body` on main once no open or reopen is in flight, a main-queue turn after the
   102	    /// last ends so AppKit has made its window — never before `applicationDidFinishLaunching`
   103	    /// (spec §11 G-47 (b)). The next turn when the shared controller is not this class. Main.
   104	    static func whenSettled(_ body: @escaping () -> Void) {
   105	        guard let controller = NSDocumentController.shared as? ProjectDocumentController else {
   106	            DispatchQueue.main.async(execute: body)
   107	            return
   108	        }
   109	        controller.settledWaiters.append(body)
   110	        controller.fireIfSettled()
   111	    }
   112

"""The capture spike's Q2(c) inventory: which menu items reach a sheet, a
modal run loop, or neither — and the checks that hold `inventory.json` to
the tree (road map 11, V1).

`inventory.json` is READ BY HAND, site first: every line the grep below
finds is traced to the menu selectors that reach it, synchronously
(`reached_from`: the action method reaches the site before it returns) or
later (`reached_after`: from a sheet or panel completion, an async hop or an
AppKit delegate callback, with the `via` line and the `gate` that must hold).
Every other live selector is read to `none`, `window` or `framework`.
The grep counts the APP-MODAL `presentError(` (road map 11's V2b) — the
`presentError(_:)` / `NSApp.presentError(_:)` that runs a modal loop — and
not the sheet form `presentError(_:modalFor:…)`, which is not modal.

  I1  every leaf of `buildMainMenu()` (the probe's `menu` mode) has its
      selector in `selectors`, and every row there names a live selector;
  I2  the grep's sites and `sites` are one-to-one, each line holding its token
      and lying in its entry's `func`; a site is FOUND BY ITS TOKEN AND ITS
      ENCLOSING FUNCTION, not its line (#166, #168): `resolve` pairs the
      inventory's sites with the grep's per (file, token, func) — `func` the
      nearest `func NAME` or `init(` declaration at or above the line — in
      line order, whenever the two counts agree, so a line added above a
      site moves its pin instead of failing it; where they disagree each pin
      stands as written. A site removed and another added in one file and
      token no longer balance unless both are in one function, so a swap
      across functions is reported (K4);
  I3  every citation is checked for content (#168). A citation is a SITE ref,
      `app/Sources/<F>.swift:<N>` naming a key of `sites` (read at its
      resolved line), or an ANCHORED ref, ``app/Sources/<F>.swift `<anchor>` ``,
      whose anchor is a piece of the line meant and occurs exactly once in
      `<F>`. Each `code` item is exactly one citation; `note`, `via`, `gate`
      and `other_caller` hold citations in prose; any other `<F>.swift:<N>`
      is a problem, as is a line citation that is not a site, an anchor
      missing or not unique, and a `reached_after` whose `via` cites nothing.
      A `modal` selector cites a line holding a loop token, a `sheet` one a
      sheet token; every `reached_from` / `reached_after` selector names a
      row; a selector in the `reached_from` of a `runModal` or loop-token
      site is `modal` (`reached_after` never forces a verdict);

# The practice project — provenance

`Practice Project.framejob` is the project Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice
Project opens as an untitled copy (spec §11 TU-6, TU-7). Everything in it was
made for Frame Job by its own generator, and is original work for Frame Job: no
third-party footage, photograph, recording or music is in it, and nothing in
it depicts a person, a logo or a brand.

- **Generator:** `tools/practice/practice_media.swift` (one scene movie) and
  `tools/practice/practice_generator.swift` (the three movies, their probes and
  `project.json`), built over `app/Sources` and run by
  `tools/practice/make_practice.py`.
- **Command:** `python3 tools/practice/make_practice.py`, which replaces the
  package and rewrites `SHA256SUMS` beside it.
- **Made:** 2026-10-31, on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80) with Xcode 26.2 (17C52).
- **Picture:** drawn frame by frame with Core Graphics and Core Text, encoded
  by AVFoundation's H.264 encoder (`AVAssetWriter`): 1280×720, 30 fps, 8 s per
  scene, an average 800 kb/s, tagged BT.709. Dawn is a peach-to-rose gradient
  with a pale sun rising; Sea a teal-to-navy gradient with three translucent
  wave bands drifting; Night an indigo-to-black gradient with a crescent and
  seeded twinkling stars. Each shows its number and name ("1 Dawn", "2 Sea",
  "3 Night") and its own source time `SS:FF`.
- **Type:** Montserrat ExtraBold and IBM Plex Mono Medium, the two OFL fonts
  already bundled in `app/Resources/Fonts` (their licences are the
  `OFL-Montserrat.txt` and `OFL-IBMPlexMono.txt` beside them); the glyphs are
  drawn into the picture, and no font file is in the package.
- **Sound:** synthesized sines, encoded by AVFoundation's AAC encoder at
  48 kHz stereo, 128 kb/s requested: a sustained triad per scene (C4 E4 G4,
  F4 A4 C5, G3 B3 D4) swelling once a second between 0.7 and 1.0 of its level,
  peaking at or under −14 dBFS, with 50 ms fades at the file's two ends.
- **No ffmpeg** in the generator or the product.
- **The project:** built through the core's own ops (`add_media`, `add_clip`,
  `trim_end`, `slip`): three 6 s clips with 1 s handles back to back on
  Track 1 from 0 to 18 s, no transition between them. Its media paths are
  placeholders under `/nonexistent/`, which the app re-anchors at open to the
  package's own `media/`.

## Digests

`SHA256SUMS` beside this file holds the SHA-256 of every file in the package
(`<sha256>  <path relative to this folder>`, sorted). `make test` runs
`tools/proof/tutorial_check.py`, which fails when a file is missing, extra or
differs from its digest, when the package is over 4,000,000 bytes, when a
media does not resolve inside the package, or when a tutorial's `needs` are not
met in it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Issue batch B44 — `close_project` and the held-path refusals (#40, spec
§11 #40), and `export_captions`' caption name rule (#43, spec §11 #43),
proved against the running app.

    python3 tools/proof/close_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. The app is a Release build
(the rows use the dev tools `snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item` and
`cancel_sheet`) at the socket, FRESH for each run: every row writes its own
package under `work/close_project/`, wiped at the start.

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **K1** — `close_project` declares exactly `{discard, project}`: `discard`
  a boolean, nothing required.
- **C1** — 60 cycles of `new_project {path: c<NN>}` → `close_project
  {project: path}`, each answering that path (compared canonically) and
  `discarded_changes: false` — well past the ~40 open documents an instance
  deadlocks at when nothing closes one.
- **C2** — every `get_project {project: c<NN>}` is refused "No open project
  is at"; `snapshot_ui {}` lists no editor window for any of them; and
  `open_project c00` answers without `already_open` (then is closed).
- **C3** — the process's thread count after C1 is under its count before C1
  plus 64; both printed.
- **D1** — `new_project`, then the autosave guard; `close_project` is refused
  with the exact unsaved-changes sentence, and `get_project` still answers.
- **D2** — the autosave guard again on a second project, then
  `close_project {discard: true}` answers `discarded_changes: true`;
  `get_project` on it is refused, and its `project.json` on disk holds no
  marker at the last attempt's `at`.
- **H1** — a text clip on its own track, `save_project`, then
  `perform_menu_item ["File", "Export…"]` puts up a sheet and `close_project`
  is refused with the exact sheet sentence; after `cancel_sheet`,
  `close_project` answers.
- **S1** — with A and B open, `save_project {project: B, path: A}` and the
  same with `path: <dir>/./<A stem>` are both refused with the exact
  held-path sentence; B's path and A's `project.json` bytes are unchanged.
- **S2** — `new_project {path: A}` is refused with the exact sentence, and
  `snapshot_ui {}`'s editor-window count is unchanged.
- **S3** (control) — `save_project {project: A, path: A}` answers `saved`. It
  runs before S1, so a build that lets S1 write B over A cannot take it.
- **E1** — with a text clip on its own track, `export_captions {path:
  <work>/chart.png}` answers a `path` ending `/chart.png.srt`; that file
  exists and `chart.srt` does not.

**The autosave guard (D1, D2).** `ProjectDocument` autosaves in place, which
clears `unsaved_changes` some seconds after an edit. Each attempt adds a
marker at a fresh `at` (600000, 1200000, 1800000), reads `get_project`, and
calls `close_project` at once only if it answers `unsaved_changes: true`; on
`false` it prints `<ID> retry <n>: autosave landed` and tries again. Three
attempts at most; all three autosaved scores the row a failure.

**A wedged instance.** Every call waits at most 60 s. After the first call
that times out the script makes no more calls, and every row left scores
"fail — instance wedged at <row>".

Rows print as `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`. Exit 0 iff no row
failed.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.error

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
from mcp import MCP, ToolError, log_beside, socket_pid, target  # noqa: E402

WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work", "close_project")
ROWS = ["T1", "K1", "C1", "C2", "C3", "D1", "D2", "H1", "S1", "S2", "S3", "E1"]
CYCLES = 60
THREAD_SLACK = 64
GUARD_ATS = [600_000, 1_200_000, 1_800_000]
states = {}


class Wedged(Exception):
    pass


class App:
    """The MCP client with the wedge rule: after the first call that times
    out, every later call raises `Wedged` without touching the instance."""

    def __init__(self, socket_path):
        self.mcp = MCP(socket_path, timeout=60)
        self.row = None
        self.wedged_at = None

    def call(self, tool, arguments):
        if self.wedged_at:
            raise Wedged(self.wedged_at)
        try:
            return self.mcp.call_with(tool, arguments)
        except ToolError:
            raise
        except (socket.timeout, TimeoutError, urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as error:
            self.wedged_at = f"{self.row} ({tool}: {type(error).__name__}: {error})"
            raise Wedged(self.wedged_at)

    def refusal(self, tool, arguments):
        """The tool's error text with the `<tool>: ` prefix `mcp.py` adds
        taken off, or None when the call answered."""
        try:
            self.call(tool, arguments)
        except ToolError as error:
            text = str(error)
            prefix = f"{tool}: "
            return text[len(prefix):] if text.startswith(prefix) else text
        return None


def score(rid, ok, detail):
    states[rid] = "pass" if ok else "fail"
    print(f"{rid} {states[rid]} — {detail}", flush=True)


def canonical(path):
    return os.path.realpath(path) if isinstance(path, str) else path


def package(name):
    return os.path.join(WORK, f"{name}.framejob")


def thread_count(pid):
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-M", "-p", str(pid)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                             timeout=20).stdout
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return None
    lines = [line for line in out.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    return len(lines) - 1 if lines else None


def editor_windows(app):
    listing = app.call("snapshot_ui", {})
    return [w for w in listing.get("windows", []) if w.get("kind") == "editor"]


def held_sentence(holder, path, tool):
    return (f"Another open project ({holder}) is at {path}, so {tool} did not write there: "
            "close_project closes it, or pass another path.")


def unsaved_sentence(name):
    return (f"{name} has unsaved changes, so close_project left it open: save_project saves "
            "them, or close_project with discard: true closes it and loses them.")


def sheet_sentence(name):
    return (f"{name} has a sheet open on its window, so close_project left it open: finish "
            "or cancel the sheet first.")


def text_clip_project(app, path):
    """A new project at `path` with one text clip on a track of its own."""
    app.call("new_project", {"path": path})
    track = app.call("get_project", {"project": path})["project"]["next_id"]
    app.call("add_track", {"project": path, "name": "Captions"})
    app.call("add_text_clip", {"project": path, "track": track, "at": 0, "duration": 1_200_000,
                               "text": {"content": "Hello"}})


def row_t1(log):
    try:
        with open(log, errors="replace") as f:
            lines = [line.rstrip() for line in f if "Frame Job: " in line]
    except OSError as error:
        score("T1", False, f"the log {log} could not be read: {error}")
        return
    score("T1", not lines, f"{len(lines)} `Frame Job: ` line(s) in {log}"
          + (f": {lines[:3]!r}" if lines else ""))


def row_k1(app):
    app.row = "K1"
    if app.wedged_at:
        raise Wedged(app.wedged_at)
    tool = app.mcp.schemas().get("close_project")
    if tool is None:
        score("K1", False, "the catalog has no close_project")
        return
    schema = tool.get("inputSchema", {})
    properties = schema.get("properties", {})
    kind = properties.get("discard", {}).get("type")
    required = schema.get("required", [])
    score("K1", set(properties) == {"discard", "project"} and kind == "boolean"
          and required == [],
          f"properties {sorted(properties)}; discard {kind!r}; required {required}")


def row_c1_c3(app, pid):
    app.row = "C1"
    before = thread_count(pid) if pid else None

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorials TU1b — the practice project, proved against the running app
(spec §11 TU-7).

    python3 tools/proof/practice_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. A Debug or Release build (P2 uses
the dev tool `perform_menu_item`), FRESH for each run, with no other project
open: the rows write under `work/practice_project/`, wiped at the start. An
untitled copy is addressed only as the frontmost document, so the rows run in
this order:

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **B1** — the instance's own `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`
  (its executable read through `lsof`, no MCP) holds exactly the files of
  `app/Resources/Practice/SHA256SUMS`, each with its digest.
- **O1** — `open_project {path: <that bundled package>}` is refused, and the
  refusal names `new_project` and `practice`.
- **P1** — `new_project {practice: true}`, then `get_project`: name "Practice
  Project", path null, `unsaved_changes` false, canvas 1280×720, three clips
  on one track at 0, 6 and 12 s, none with a `transition_in`, no
  `missing_media`, and every media path inside the bundled package's
  `media/`.
- **P2** — `perform_menu_item ["Help", "Tutorials", "Open Practice Project"]`
  opens one more editor window, and `get_project` (now that copy, the
  frontmost) answers the same three clips, named "Practice Project".
- **P3** — `render_frame` of P2's copy at 1, 7 and 13 s writes three PNGs,
  pairwise byte-different (Dawn, Sea, Night).
- **P4** — on P2's copy (no `project` argument): `set_audio` on its first
  clip (volume 0.5), then `save_project {path: work/practice_project/saved}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "saved"; the saved package's `media/`
  holds Dawn.mov, Sea.mov and Night.mov byte-equal to the bundle's; its
  `project.json` names each media at `<saved>/media/<file>`, none inside the
  app, with no bookmark. Then `close_project {project: <saved>, discard:
  true}`.
- **R1** — `open_project {path: <saved>}`: name "saved", no `missing_media`,
  every media path inside `<saved>/media/`, the first clip's volume 0.5;
  closed by its path. P1's copy, now the only document, is closed with
  `close_project {discard: true}`.
- **P5** — `new_project {practice: true, path: work/practice_project/direct}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "direct", and its package passes P4's
  `media/` and `project.json` checks; closed by its path.
- **N1** — the bundled package's files still equal `SHA256SUMS`, with no
  file added.

Rows print as `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`. Exit 0 iff no row
failed.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "practice"))
import proof_app  # noqa: E402
from make_practice import PACKAGE_NAME, PRACTICE, SUMS  # noqa: E402
from mcp import MCP, ToolError, log_beside, socket_pid, target  # noqa: E402

WORK = HERE / "work" / "practice_project"
ROWS = ["T1", "B1", "O1", "P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "R1", "P5", "N1"]
SECOND = 600_000
FILES = ("Dawn.mov", "Sea.mov", "Night.mov")
states = {}


def score(rid, ok, detail):
    states[rid] = "pass" if ok else "fail"
    print(f"{rid} {states[rid]} — {detail}", flush=True)


def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def real(path):
    return os.path.realpath(str(path))


def inside(path, folder):
    root = real(folder).rstrip("/") + "/"
    return isinstance(path, str) and real(path).startswith(root)


def recorded_sums():
    rows = {}
    for row in (PRACTICE / SUMS).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        digest, _, name = row.partition("  ")
        rows[name] = digest
    return rows


def bundle_problems(resources):
    """`resources` (an app's Contents/Resources) against SHA256SUMS."""
    recorded = recorded_sums()
    package = resources / PACKAGE_NAME
    present = {path.relative_to(resources).as_posix(): path for path in package.rglob("*")
               if path.is_file()} if package.is_dir() else {}
    out = [f"{name} missing" for name in sorted(set(recorded) - set(present))]
    out += [f"{name} extra" for name in sorted(set(present) - set(recorded))]
    out += [f"{name} differs" for name in sorted(set(recorded) & set(present))
            if sha(present[name]) != recorded[name]]
    return out, len(present)


def clips_of(answer):
    return sorted(answer["project"]["clips"], key=lambda clip: clip["start"])


def clip_problems(answer):
    clips = clips_of(answer)
    out = []
    if [clip["start"] for clip in clips] != [0, 6 * SECOND, 12 * SECOND]:
        out.append(f"starts {[clip['start'] for clip in clips]}")
    if len({clip["track"] for clip in clips}) != 1:
        out.append("clips on more than one track")
    if any(clip.get("transition_in") for clip in clips):
        out.append("a clip has a transition_in")
    return out


def media_paths(project):
    return {Path(media["path"]).name: media for media in project["media"]}


def package_problems(saved, bundle_package, app_bundle):
    """P4's checks of a saved practice copy at `saved`."""
    out = []
    for name in FILES:
        copy = saved / "media" / name
        if not copy.is_file():
            out.append(f"media/{name} absent")
        elif sha(copy) != sha(bundle_package / "media" / name):
            out.append(f"media/{name} differs from the bundle's")
    project = json.loads((saved / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for media in project["media"]:
        path = media.get("path")
        want = real(saved / "media" / Path(path or "").name)
        if real(path or "") != want:
            out.append(f"media {media['id']} at {path!r}, not {want}")
        if inside(path, app_bundle):
            out.append(f"media {media['id']} inside the app")
        if media.get("bookmark"):
            out.append(f"media {media['id']} has a bookmark")
    if len(project["media"]) != 3:
        out.append(f"{len(project['media'])} media")
    return out


def editors(mcp):
    return [w for w in mcp.call("snapshot_ui").get("windows", []) if w.get("kind") == "editor"]


def refusal(mcp, tool, arguments):
    try:
        mcp.call_with(tool, arguments)
    except ToolError as error:
        return str(error)
    return None


def run(mcp, log, app_bundle):
    resources = app_bundle / "Contents" / "Resources"
    bundle_package = resources / PACKAGE_NAME
    media_folder = bundle_package / "media"

    lines = [line.rstrip() for line in open(log, errors="replace") if "Frame Job: " in line]
    score("T1", not lines, f"{len(lines)} `Frame Job: ` line(s) in {log}")

    problems, count = bundle_problems(resources)
    score("B1", not problems and count > 0,
          f"{count} files in {bundle_package}; {problems or 'all equal SHA256SUMS'}")

    said = refusal(mcp, "open_project", {"path": str(bundle_package)})
    score("O1", said is not None and "new_project" in said and "practice" in said,
          f"open_project answered {said!r}")

    made = mcp.call("new_project", practice=True)
    first = mcp.call("get_project")
    canvas = first["project"]["canvas"]
    wrong = clip_problems(first)
    paths = [media["path"] for media in first["project"]["media"]]
    score("P1", first["name"] == "Practice Project" and first["path"] is None
          and first["unsaved_changes"] is False and (canvas["width"], canvas["height"])
          == (1280, 720) and not wrong and "missing_media" not in first
          and len(paths) == 3 and all(inside(path, media_folder) for path in paths)
          and made["project"]["name"] == "Practice Project",
          f"name {first['name']!r}, path {first['path']}, unsaved {first['unsaved_changes']}, "
          f"canvas {canvas['width']}×{canvas['height']}, clips {wrong or 'at 0/6/12 s'}, "
          f"missing {first.get('missing_media')}, media {paths}")

    before = len(editors(mcp))
    menu = mcp.call("perform_menu_item", path=["Help", "Tutorials", "Open Practice Project"])
    after = len(editors(mcp))
    second = mcp.call("get_project")
    score("P2", after == before + 1 and second["name"] == "Practice Project"
          and not clip_problems(second) and second["path"] is None,
          f"editor windows {before} → {after}; frontmost {second['name']!r}, "
          f"clips {clip_problems(second) or 'at 0/6/12 s'}; menu answered "
          f"{json.dumps(menu, ensure_ascii=False)[:160]}")

    frames = []
    for seconds in (1, 7, 13):
        out = WORK / f"frame-{seconds}.png"
        mcp.call("render_frame", t=seconds * SECOND, path=str(out))
        frames.append(out.read_bytes() if out.is_file() else b"")
    distinct = all(frames) and len({sha_bytes(b) for b in frames}) == 3
    score("P3", distinct, f"{[len(b) for b in frames]} bytes at 1, 7, 13 s; pairwise "
          f"{'different' if distinct else 'NOT different'}")

    saved = WORK / "saved.framejob"
    first_clip = clips_of(second)[0]["id"]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorials TU1b — the practice project, proved against the running app
(spec §11 TU-7).

    python3 tools/proof/practice_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. A Debug or Release build (P2 uses
the dev tool `perform_menu_item`), FRESH for each run, with no other project
open: the rows write under `work/practice_project/`, wiped at the start. An
untitled copy is addressed only as the frontmost document, so the rows run in
this order:

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **B1** — the instance's own `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`
  (its executable read through `lsof`, no MCP) holds exactly the files of
  `app/Resources/Practice/SHA256SUMS`, each with its digest.
- **O1** — `open_project {path: <that bundled package>}` is refused, and the
  refusal names `new_project` and `practice`.
- **P1** — `new_project {practice: true}`, then `get_project`: name "Practice
  Project", path null, `unsaved_changes` false, canvas 1280×720, three clips
  on one track at 0, 6 and 12 s, none with a `transition_in`, no
  `missing_media`, and every media path inside the bundled package's
  `media/`.
- **P2** — `perform_menu_item ["Help", "Tutorials", "Open Practice Project"]`
  opens one more editor window, and `get_project` (now that copy, the
  frontmost) answers the same three clips, named "Practice Project".
- **P3** — `render_frame` of P2's copy at 1, 7 and 13 s writes three PNGs,
  pairwise byte-different (Dawn, Sea, Night).
- **P4** — on P2's copy (no `project` argument): `set_audio` on its first
  clip (volume 0.5), then `save_project {path: work/practice_project/saved}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "saved"; the saved package's `media/`
  holds Dawn.mov, Sea.mov and Night.mov byte-equal to the bundle's; its
  `project.json` names each media at `<saved>/media/<file>`, none inside the
  app, with no bookmark. Then `close_project {project: <saved>, discard:
  true}`.
- **R1** — `open_project {path: <saved>}`: name "saved", no `missing_media`,
  every media path inside `<saved>/media/`, the first clip's volume 0.5;
  closed by its path. P1's copy, now the only document, is closed with
  `close_project {discard: true}`.
- **P5** — `new_project {practice: true, path: work/practice_project/direct}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "direct", and its package passes P4's
  `media/` and `project.json` checks; closed by its path.
- **N1** — the bundled package's files still equal `SHA256SUMS`, with no
  file added.

failed.

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "practice"))

ROWS = ["T1", "B1", "O1", "P1", "P2", "P3", "P4", "R1", "P5", "N1"]

states = {}


def score(rid, ok, detail):
    states[rid] = "pass" if ok else "fail"

def sha(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def real(path):
    return os.path.realpath(str(path))


def inside(path, folder):
    root = real(folder).rstrip("/") + "/"
    return isinstance(path, str) and real(path).startswith(root)


def recorded_sums():
    rows = {}
    for row in (PRACTICE / SUMS).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        digest, _, name = row.partition("  ")
        rows[name] = digest
    return rows


def bundle_problems(resources):
    """`resources` (an app's Contents/Resources) against SHA256SUMS."""
    recorded = recorded_sums()

               if path.is_file()} if package.is_dir() else {}

    out += [f"{name} extra" for name in sorted(set(present) - set(recorded))]
    out += [f"{name} differs" for name in sorted(set(recorded) & set(present))

    return out, len(present)

          and made["project"]["name"] == "Practice Project",

          f"saved {answer.get('saved')}, name {answer['project']['name']!r}; "
          f"{problems or 'media carried and named inside the package'}")
    mcp.call("close_project", project=str(saved), discard=True)

    opened = mcp.call("open_project", path=str(saved))
    back = mcp.call("get_project", project=str(saved))
    volume = next(clip for clip in back["project"]["clips"]
                  if clip["id"] == first_clip).get("audio", {}).get("volume")
    outside = [media["path"] for media in back["project"]["media"]
               if not inside(media["path"], saved / "media")]
    score("R1", opened["project"]["name"] == "saved" and "missing_media" not in back
          and not outside and volume == 0.5,
          f"name {opened['project']['name']!r}, missing {back.get('missing_media')}, "
          f"outside media/ {outside}, first clip volume {volume}")
    mcp.call("close_project", project=str(saved), discard=True)
    mcp.call("close_project", discard=True)

    direct = WORK / "direct.framejob"
    answer = mcp.call("new_project", practice=True, path=str(direct))
    problems = package_problems(direct, bundle_package, app_bundle)

content.content:
Opening a `.framejob` package opens that project (a double-click on a package always opens it in Frame Job). If it is already open, its window comes forward.

Dropping several files at once on a window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon opens each one as its own untitled project. Only `.framejob` packages and the movie, sound and picture types File ▸ Open… lists are taken; anything else dropped there is ignored. To add files to the project you already have open, drop them on the [Media tab](#the-media-tab) instead.

*Agents:* `open_project` (takes a `path` to a package, movie, sound file or picture; answers `already_open: true` when that file is already open).

### New Project

**File ▸ New Project** (⌘N) opens a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project". Change the size and rate afterwards on the Document tab (see [The Document tab](#the-document-tab-canvas-settings)).

*Agents:* `new_project` (an optional `path` saves it there straight away; without one it stays an untitled draft).

### The Welcome window

25:*Agents:* `open_project` (takes a `path` to a package, movie, sound file or picture; answers `already_open: true` when that file is already open).
31:*Agents:* `new_project` (an optional `path` saves it there straight away; without one it stays an untitled draft).
60:*Agents:* `save_project` (a `path` is required the first time and always means Save As), `close_project` (refused when `get_project` reports `unsaved_changes` unless `discard: true`, and refused while a sheet is open), `get_project` (the whole project as JSON plus the playhead, selection, in/out range, `unsaved_changes` and `missing_media`). `new_project` adds `.framejob` to a `path` that lacks it. `new_project` and `save_project` refuse a path another open project holds (close that one first) or one a window is still opening.

Each clip shows its scene's name and its own source time, and plays a held chord, so a volume change or a cross dissolve is easy to see and hear.

It opens as an untitled copy in a window titled "Practice Project", so the copy inside Frame Job is never changed. Edit it as you like; **File ▸ Save** asks where to save it, and the window then takes the file's name. A saved copy carries its media inside its package (the three movies are copied into its `media/` folder), so it opens on its own wherever it is moved. Open Practice Project again for a fresh copy.

Opening the copy inside Frame Job's app from the Finder (through Show Package Contents) opens a fresh untitled copy too, never the original.

*Agents:* `new_project {practice: true}` (with `path`, the copy is saved there, its media inside it). `open_project` refuses a path inside Frame Job's app.

content.content:
## Agent connections

Whether an MCP client refetches its tool list when a stdio server says it
changed (road map 14's MC1, question 3). The fixture is the spike's stub
server, which has two tools only after it sends
`notifications/tools/list_changed`. Run
`python3 tools/proof/mc1_spike/mc1_spike.py --only q3` once first: it writes
`tools/proof/work/mc1_spike/q3/ac-mcp.json`, a scratch configuration naming
the stub with `--mode during-call`, whose log is
`tools/proof/work/mc1_spike/q3/ac-stub.jsonl`. Each run is your own spend
on your own account, never the spike's.

**AC-1 — Claude Code refetches after `list_changed`**
- **Do:** 1. Delete `ac-stub.jsonl` if it is there. 2. In a terminal, `claude --mcp-config tools/proof/work/mc1_spike/q3/ac-mcp.json --strict-mcp-config`. 3. Ask it to call the `probe_wait` tool of the `mc1-stub` server, and when that answers, to call `probe_new`. 4. Quit, and read `ac-stub.jsonl`.
- **Expect:** among the log's lines (it also holds `notifications/initialized` and any other calls the client makes), in this order: `initialize`, `tools/list`, the `tools/call` of `probe_wait`, the `"dir": "out"` notification, then a second `tools/list`; then a `tools/call` of `probe_new`. The log holds only what the stub received and the notifications it sent, never its answers, so that `probe_new` answered `probe_new answered` is seen in the client.
- **Answer:** did a second `tools/list` follow the notification, and was `probe_new` callable in the same session?
- **Source:** road map 14 MC1 (q3, rows T1–T3 and D1).

**AC-2 — Claude Desktop refetches after `list_changed`**
- **Do:** 1. Delete `ac-stub.jsonl` if it is there. 2. Copy the `mc1-stub` entry of `ac-mcp.json` into the `mcpServers` of Claude Desktop's `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` and restart Claude Desktop. 3. In a new chat, ask it to call `probe_wait`, then `probe_new`. 4. Read `ac-stub.jsonl`. 5. Remove the `mc1-stub` entry and restart Claude Desktop.
- **Expect:** as AC-1: a second `tools/list` after the notification, and `probe_new` called and answered.
- **Answer:** did a second `tools/list` follow the notification, and was `probe_new` callable in the same chat?
- **Source:** road map 14 MC1 (q3, rows T1–T3 and D1).

**AC-3 — Claude Code reaches Frame Job through `framejob-mcp`**
- **Do:** 1. `make app`, then `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/mcp_proxy_proof.py` once: it writes `tools/proof/work/mcp-proxy/ac-mcp.json`, a scratch configuration whose `framejob` server is the tree's Release `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`, with no env. 2. Quit Frame Job (every copy). 3. In a terminal, `claude --mcp-config tools/proof/work/mcp-proxy/ac-mcp.json --strict-mcp-config`. 4. Ask it to list the `framejob` server's tools (`/mcp`). 5. Ask it to call `get_project`. 6. Quit Claude Code, and quit the Frame Job it opened.
- **Expect:** step 4 lists Frame Job's tools with no Frame Job launched (the Dock shows none). Step 5 opens Frame Job in the background — the terminal keeps focus — and the call answers in Frame Job's own words (with no project open, "No project is open…"). Per MC1's q3, a running Frame Job newer than the bundle the proxy came from shows its own tools after the first call; whether Claude Code refetches on `list_changed` is AC-1's question.
- **Answer:** were the tools listed before Frame Job ran, and did the first call open Frame Job without taking focus from the terminal and answer?
- **Source:** road map 14 MC3 (`mcp_proxy_proof.py` X1, X2; spec §11 MC-3, MC-4).

**AC-4 — Copy MCP Command's line registers Frame Job with Claude Code**
- **Do:** 1. Open the Frame Job you use (an installed copy, or the tree's Release build), choose Frame Job ▸ Settings…, and under MCP press Copy MCP Command. 2. Paste the line into Terminal and run it. 3. Run `claude mcp list`.
- **Expect:** step 2 answers that `framejob` was added; step 3 lists `framejob` with the pasted helper path and shows it connected.
- **Answer:** did the pasted line run as it stood, and does `claude mcp list` show `framejob` connected?
- **Source:** `agent_socket_proof.py` K13; `settings_layout_probe.py` L10; spec §11 MC-7.

**AC-5 — A person's own import still asks while an agent's call runs**
- **Do:** 1. Launch Frame Job from Terminal as in CLAUDE.md's "Verifying a build", adding `-RCFFmpegImport ask` to its arguments (ffmpeg installed), and open a project with a few seconds of media on the timeline. 2. In a second Terminal tab, in the repository, start an export over MCP: `python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0, "tools/proof"); from mcp import MCP; print(MCP("<dir>/agent.sock").call("export", preset="h264", path="/tmp/ac5.mp4"))'`. 3. While it runs, drag onto the timeline from the Finder an `.mkv` whose video the built-in copy cannot carry, so it goes on to the ffmpeg question (since #216-R an H.264, VP9 or AV1 Matroska opens with no question; make one with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=duration=2 -c:v mpeg4 /tmp/ac5.mkv`). 4. Cancel the question.
- **Expect:** the conversion question ("Frame Job cannot open …", Repackage or Convert) appears for the dragged file while the export is still being written; the export finishes either way.
- **Answer:** did the question appear during the agent's export?
- **Source:** road map 14 MC4 (spec §11 MC-5: a click still asks; `agent_socket_proof.py` K12 holds the tool call's half).

## The name

**NAME-1 — Finder opens a `.framejob` with Frame Job; the Debug app stays the Alternate**
- **Do:** 1. `make app` and `make app-debug`. 2. Rename a saved project's package to end in `.framejob`. 3. Double-click it in the Finder. 4. Right-click it and open the Open With submenu.
- **Expect:** step 3 opens it in Frame Job (the Release build), not Frame Job Debug; step 4 lists Frame Job as the default and Frame Job Debug as another choice.
- **Answer:** did the double-click open Frame Job, and does Open With list Frame Job Debug as an alternate?
- **Source:** spec §11 NM-3, V-5.

**NAME-2 — The Dock icon, the About panel and the document icon carry the Frame Job mark**
- **Do:** 1. `make app`. 2. Open the Release app from the Finder and look at the Dock icon. 3. Choose Frame Job ▸ About Frame Job, in Light and then in Dark. 4. Look at a saved `.framejob` package in the Finder's icon view at a large size, and in Get Info.
- **Expect:** the Dock shows the cream rounded tile with four green corner brackets, a yellow frame and a coral playhead; About shows the same mark with no tile, sharp-edged, in both appearances; the package's document icon carries the new icon. An old two-block icon after a rebuild is the icon cache: log out and back in, then look again before answering.
- **Answer:** do the Dock, the About panel (Light and Dark) and the package's document icon all show the new viewfinder mark?
- **Source:** spec §11 NM-11, rename R2.

## Published build

newest input (once per socket and pid; `lsof` names its executable, `ps -o
lstart=` its start, to the second), or whose product is refused, never by
the executable's mtime ("relaunch pid N after `make app-debug`: <file>
(modified …) is newer than the instance (started …)"). With no pid holding the socket it says so on
stderr and does not refuse. The inputs are `app/`, `agent/`, `core/src`,

import AppKit

#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
/// `perform_menu_item`'s allow-table (road map 11's V2b): one row per
/// selector in `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`, in its order, with
/// the verdict V1's inventory read for it — `none` (spelled `.plain`, so no
/// `Optional.none` ambiguity), `sheet`, `window`, `modal` or `framework`.
///
/// **A mirror, held to its source by the proof.** `v2_menu.py`'s H2 compares
/// this table to the inventory in both directions and H1 holds the inventory
/// to the live menu, so a menu item added without a row here is refused as
/// `unclassified` by the tool and fails the proof until both are written.
/// `UIMenu.refusal(for:)` refuses `framework` and `modal` rows by name and
/// every selector with no row.
extension UIMenu {
    static let verdicts: [String: Verdict] = [
        "showAboutPanel:": .window,
        "showSettings:": .window,
        "hide:": .framework,
        "hideOtherApplications:": .framework,
        "unhideAllApplications:": .framework,
        "terminate:": .framework,
        "newProject:": .modal,
        "newRecording:": .window,
        "pauseOrResumeRecording:": .plain,
        "openDocument:": .framework,
        "clearRecentDocuments:": .framework,
        "performClose:": .framework,

gh issue create --label ai-drafted --label low-priority --title "An untitled practice copy restored from an autosave after the app moved has missing media" --body "Tutorials TU1b (spec §11 TU-7, \`designs/tutorials.md\` Record). A practice copy (Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project, or \`new_project {practice: true}\`) references the bundled movies inside \`Frame Job.app/Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob/media/\` until it is saved. A saved copy carries them into its own package (\`ProjectDocument+PracticeMedia.swift\`), but an UNTITLED copy's autosave-elsewhere package does not: \`write(to:…)\` skips \`.autosaveElsewhereOperation\` by design.

So if the app is quit with an edited, never-saved practice copy, then moved, renamed, updated in place or run translocated, and the copy is restored on the next launch, its media paths name the old app location and the clips show as missing until Relink… (or until the person reopens the practice project).

Possible fixes: re-anchor media under any \`Practice Project.framejob/media/\` path at the current \`PracticeProject.bundledURL\` on read (the \`repairingMedia\` step), or carry the practice media into autosave-elsewhere packages too.

Owed by TU1b as accepted residue (spec §11 TU-7's \"Risk accepted\").

# TU1b — implementation notes

## What was done

Followed the spec's Approach in order.

1. **Decisions first.** `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md`: TU-2 (3) now defines `has_sound` (an `audio` group) and `has_pixels` (a `video` group on a clip that is not an adjustment); new **TU-7** (the package, the untitled copy, a saved copy owns its media, no open in place, the checker, the accepted autosave-elsewhere risk). Index rows in `11-decisions/README.md` (Lines 147, TU-7 row), `designs/spec/README.md` Lines cells (07.9a 489, 09 208, `11-decisions/` 14972 in 34 files), §7.9a (`open_project`'s refusal, `new_project {path?, practice?}`), §9 (Help: Frame Job Help; Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project; Graphics Reference).
2. **Extractor nits** (`tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py`, still 3.9-safe; `/usr/bin/python3` run printed `5 tutorials in 5 pages`): (1) `_refused` claims the following list's lines when a closed tutorial comment is refused (text after `-->`, bad JSON, no string id, unknown key); (2) `_step` refuses an item holding `<!-- tutorial`; (4) `parse_page` now wraps a private `_parse_page` that also answers each tutorial's comment line, and `parse_guide` reports a duplicate there. `parse_page`/`parse_guide` signatures and output unchanged. Nit (3) fixed in `tutorial_check.py`'s docstring. `_list_start` is a small private helper shared by the normal path and the refused path.
3. **Swift.** `TutorialClipFacts.swift` (§A), `PracticeProject.swift` (§B), `AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift` (§C), `ProjectDocument+PracticeMedia.swift` (§F's `write` override), `+CacheSaves` funnel (note/clear destination, `displayName = nil` on success), `ProjectDocumentController` redirect (after the `.fjgraphic` branch, before `began`), `MediaConsolidator.plan` relinks a carried practice file (`carriedPracticeFile`), `AppDelegate+Menus` one line, `AppDelegate.validateMenuItem` arm, `UIMenuTable` row, `inventory.json` selector row + site, `AgentServer+Project` (`practice` arg, `open_project` refusal), `AgentCatalog` (587 lines).
4. **Generator.** `tools/practice/practice_media.swift` (393 lines), `practice_generator.swift` (142), `make_practice.py` (159). Ran it; package 1,497,141 bytes (Dawn.mov 438,263, Sea.mov 416,277, Night.mov 637,027, project.json 5,574). Sea's audio measured by ffmpeg volumedetect: max −14.9 dB. `PROVENANCE.md`, `project.yml` entry.
5. **Probe §D + `check_practice`**, fixtures (`facts.json` practice block, `tutorial_fixtures/practice/`), 5 new selftest cases.
6. **graphics_menu_probe/proof M3.**
7. **`practice_project_proof.py`** (T1, B1, O1, P1–P5, R1, N1).
8. Guide pages, manual checks (TUT-1, TUT-2), developing.md, Makefile comment, proof README, road-map §5a line and Record.

## Deviations from the spec

- **P4/P5/R1's name check.** The spec says `project.name` "saved" / "direct". On this host AppKit's `displayName` for a saved package is `saved.framejob` (the extension is shown), as it is for every saved project. The proof accepts the file's name with or without `.framejob` (`file_named`) and still refuses "Practice Project". The docstring and README say so.
- **Mutant "the funnel's `displayName = nil` removed" SURVIVED.** With the line removed, P4 and P5 still answered `saved.framejob` / `direct.framejob`: AppKit itself drops a set `displayName` when a save gives the document its file (Save As through `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)`), at least on macOS 26.5.1. The line stays as the spec wrote it (it is harmless and covers any path where AppKit does not), but no instrument can make it fail today; objection 1's premise did not hold on this host. Recorded in the road map's Record.
- **The generator asserts a little more than the spec lists**: each clip's start, its 6 s duration and its 1 s source `in`, beside the three-clips/no-transition/trial-dissolve asserts — the handles the Out of scope says "the generator asserts".
- **The media writer pumps through `requestMediaDataWhenReady`** on two serial queues (one per input) rather than a polling loop: the first, polled version stalled ("the writer stopped taking data: timed out") on Dawn.mov. The audio is appended in 1,024-frame buffers.
- **AAC bitrate.** 128 kb/s is requested (`AVEncoderBitRateKey`); ffmpeg reports Sea's audio stream at 59 kb/s, the encoder's own choice on a held chord. PROVENANCE.md says "128 kb/s requested".
- `PracticeProject.open()` checks for the bundle inside step 3's `do` (after the untitled document is made), as the spec's order has it; an absent bundle closes the document it made.
- `PracticeProject` and `+PracticeMedia` spell `"media"` and `"project.json"` as literals, because `ProjectDocument.mediaDirectoryName` / `projectFileName` are `private` and `ProjectDocument.swift` is not to be edited.
- `practice_project_proof.py` reads the instance's bundle through `proof_app._instance(pid)` (the executable `lsof` names), not a new helper.

## Files touched outside the Files list

- `/private/tmp/...` scratch scripts only (edit helpers); nothing else in the repo. The Debug product's bundle was contaminated by mutant 7 (`cache/` written into `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`, which N1 caught); that `cache/` folder was removed from `build/Build/Products/Debug/…` after the mutant run.

## Residue

- Filed **#425** (`ai-drafted`, `low-priority`): an untitled practice copy restored from an autosave elsewhere after the app moved has missing media until Relink.

## CLAUDE.md edits owed (not applied)

- Root `CLAUDE.md` file map: a `tools/practice/` row (the generator: `practice_generator.swift`, `practice_media.swift`, `make_practice.py`; regenerate with `python3 tools/practice/make_practice.py`) and an `app/Resources/Practice/` row (`Practice Project.framejob`, bundled as `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`; `SHA256SUMS` and `PROVENANCE.md`, not bundled).
- Root `CLAUDE.md` `make test` line: `tutorial_check.py`'s clause also covers the practice project's needs, media and `SHA256SUMS`.
- `app/CLAUDE.md`: entries for `TutorialClipFacts.swift` (the clip filter's five keys per clip, `matches`) and `PracticeProject.swift` (locate/read/open the practice copy, `isInsideApp`, the bundled-media queries and the save funnel's destination record) under Tutorials; `+PracticeMedia` in the `ProjectDocument.swift` family line (a practice copy's write carries the bundled media into the package it writes); `+Tutorials` in the AppDelegate family line (Help ▸ Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project); `ProjectDocumentController.swift`'s redirect (a URL inside the app opens a practice copy); `+CacheSaves`' role now also the practice destination record; `MediaConsolidator.swift`'s carried-practice-file relink.
- `app/CLAUDE.md` Hygiene's `DispatchQueue` seam list: `AppDelegate.openPracticeProject`'s one `DispatchQueue.main.async { NSApp.presentError(error) }` hop (spec §C asks for it so the menu verdict is `window`), and `practice_media.swift`'s two writer queues are a dev tool's, not the app's.

## Still failing

Nothing (see 04-checks.txt).
